keyRules: Maximum altitude: 122 m (400 ft) above ground level (AGL)
Registration in the DGAC’s online registration system is mandatory for every drone of 250 g or more (up to 250 kg), with no exception based on use
The registration number or QR code must be visible on the drone
Always carry your DGAC certificate with you when operating in public spaces
Always keep the drone within direct line of sight (VLOS)

Open category (recreational use): drone under 4 kg, pilot at least 14 years old (with adult supervision) who has reviewed the DGAC’s induction material; the drone must have active remote identification and a geofencing function
Daytime flight; at night (and during civil twilight) only if the drone has visible position or anti-collision lights — with night vision systems, a visual observer is required
🚫 GALÁPAGOS: recreational, private, or tourist use of drones PROHIBITED in land and marine protected areas

🚫 Controlled aerodromes: flying is prohibited within a rectangle extending 600 m on each side of the runway centerline up to 3 km from each threshold and within the approach/departure cones up to 5 km, unless the DGAC grants a special UAS flight authorization; in the rest of the 5 km radius, max. 40 m AGL and only with authorization from or coordination with the aerodrome operator. Uncontrolled aerodromes: 1.8 km; heliports: 0.9 km (unless authorized by or coordinated with their operator). The open category may not fly in FRZ zones.
Commercial operation: requires additional certification + overflight permits depending on the area
Do not fly over people not involved in the operation

Urban or residential areas: flying is prohibited within 30 m (horizontally and vertically) of people not involved in the operation and of any building, unless the DGAC grants a special UAS flight authorization; also comply with local ordinances
importantNotes: 📋 RDAC 101 (effective as of December 2024): new UAS regulation approved by the DGAC Standards Committee on October 24, 2024. Applies to ALL individuals (recreational, private, professional) operating drones with a maximum takeoff weight (MTOW) of up to 250 kg.

🆔 REGISTRATION: every drone of 250 g or more (up to 250 kg) must be registered online with the DGAC. The system issues a certificate with a unique number and QR code; the number or QR code must be marked on the drone and on the remote controller.

🐢 GALÁPAGOS: Resolution MAE-PNG/DIR-2026-0006-RM (in effect since January 16, 2026) prohibits recreational, private, or tourist use of drones in land and marine protected areas. Only the following are authorized, with a permit from the Park: scientific research, search and rescue, environmental management and monitoring, and commercial, news, educational, or cultural filming/photography. Non-compliance leads to administrative, criminal, and civil action.

✈️ FOREIGN TOURISTS: RDAC 101 also applies to foreigners. To register a drone of 250 g or more, the regulation requires being 18 years of age or older and an Ecuadorian citizen or resident foreigner; the portal accepts passports, but check with the DGAC before traveling whether you can register as a non-resident tourist. In the Galápagos protected areas, recreational use is prohibited.

🌳 OTHER NATIONAL PARKS: Cotopaxi, Yasuní, Cajas, Sangay, and other protected areas managed by the Ministry of the Environment require specific permits for drones. Check with the Ministry of the Environment and the relevant park before flying.

fields.disclaimerText: Always check the DGAC’s official sources before flying. This app is a tool, not a legal authority. Ecuador enforces RDAC 101 (effective as of December 2024)—drones of 250 g or more must be registered in the DGAC’s online registration system. The Galápagos Islands have special restrictions.
